hero.headline: THE REMATCH FRANCE NEVER WANTED
hero.standfirst: Qatar 2022, semi-final: France 2, Morocco 0 — and a football continent left wondering what might have been. Tonight in Boston they meet again, one round earlier, with France unbeaten and scoring freely, and a Morocco side that has conceded just once in the knockouts. The last eight starts with its heavyweight bout.

todaySub: Quarter-final 1 of 4 — the winner is two games from the final

today.preview: France have been the tournament's most complete attacking side: five wins from five, none needing extra time, 14 goals, and the Mbappé–Dembélé axis purring. Morocco have built their run the other way — a defensive wall that dismantled Canada 3–0 and has conceded once in the knockouts. In Qatar they made history reaching the semi-final; France ended it, 2–0. Tonight is the chance to rewrite that ending, without the injured Ismael Saibari.

keyMan.name: Achraf Hakimi
keyMan.line: Captain of the wall. Born in Madrid, made in Paris, and the man who must somehow patrol the wing where Mbappé — his old PSG teammate — does his worst.

factors.label: FORM
factors.text: France: five wins from five, 14 scored, never needed extra time. Morocco: one goal conceded in the knockouts and a 3–0 dismantling of Canada.

factors.label: HEAD-TO-HEAD
factors.text: The 2022 semi-final is the reference point: France won 2–0 in Qatar on the night Morocco's historic run ended. Most of both cores were there.

factors.label: FITNESS & FATIGUE
factors.text: Morocco are without forward Ismael Saibari, a genuine loss to their transition game. France report a clean bill and have played the fewest hard minutes of any quarter-finalist.

factors.label: WHERE THE MONEY IS
factors.text: Kalshi's live market ($1.7m traded): France 62%, the draw 25%, Morocco 15% in regulation. A full quarter of the money expects this level after 90 minutes.

prediction.verdict: Morocco will make it ugly, and the draw price says the market respects that. But France's front line is the one force in this tournament no block has contained, and Saibari's absence blunts the counter Morocco would need. France — later than their fans would like.
